Not a Walker supporter, but I can summarize the viewpoint since it's hardly restricted to Walker: if you focus all your time on why <insert other race or group> is responsible for all your problems, you'll never improve the situation, because they aren't the cause of /all/ your problems. It doesn't matter whether they're white people, or the wealthy, or our reptilian overlords who're to blame. Focusing on what you can change yourself is a good first step.

It's weird that this early in the election cycle, people already have laundry lists of criticisms of particular candidates to inject into conversation

This idea has been around for a very long time. Self-improvement comes from the individual's efforts. No one else can make you a better person.

In terms of race relations, Walker's approach was first encapsulated by Booker T. Washington with his famous "Let Down Your Bucket Where You Are" speech. He argued that blacks must be allowed to improve themselves, and that in if they are allowed to do so then they would inevitably reach parity with the other races. The flip-side argument was endorsed by others like W.E.B. DuBois, who argued that blacks needed positive support and reparations if they were to ever reach equality with the other races. MLK, Jr. had begun to move towards this position later in life; he wrote in "Where Do We Go From Here" that you can't unchain a slave and expect him to run the same race as somebody who has been free from birth. The newly-freed slave has to be supported with government programs and wealth transfers.

"Our Constitution is color-blind" is essentially the motto of the first position. Everyone should be treated the same, regardless of race. "Affirmative Action" is essentially the motto of the second. People who have been historically oppressed and disadvantaged should be prioritized in education and job opportunities in order to help them reach parity with the non-disadvantaged.

Walker saying "don't focus on racial discord or you'll only create more" essentially means that affirmative action programs create blowback and increase racial resentment, and that we should instead strive towards a color-blind society and racial integration.

People of principle and goodwill can argue for either position.

Last week my friend's father died in prison (he was doing time for financial fraud). He was diagnosed with lung cancer in prison. Prison doctors didn't do shit, and you'd be lucky if they allowed him to take some aspirin. Prison officials didn't give two fucks about him, and the guy was in absolute agony. My friend pleaded with the Ministry of Interior to transfer him to a medical prison, and after some time they finally agreed.

Thing about medical wards, are they are pretty much your final stop, and in there all they do is give you water, some food, and just wait until you die. The medical care is nonexistent there, and they didn't even let my friend send him a package with pain killers, and other medicines to ease her father's pain. The man died in complete agony, alone, with nobody to look after him in his final days.

I've got plenty of horror stories involving our prisons. Fuck our penal system, and everyone who runs it.

Okay, here's another one for you.

In extremely harsh (even by Russian standards) prisons, during the first couple of days, prisoners are required to go through a special procedure:

  1. They place you in a single cell with no windows, and the only source of light is light bulbs.

  2. Every time the guard is about to come in, he knocks on the door, and you need to immediately run to the middle of the cell, get on your knees, face the wall, and put your hands behind your back. They can and do knock at any time, even when you're asleep, and God forbid you're not ready in seconds! Otherwise your ass is toast, they'll beat on you till they think you've had enough.

  3. You need to clean up your cell to an absolute shine. At any given moment the guard will come in and inspect it, and if he finds even a tiniest spec of dust, you get your ass kicked. Obviously all of this had nothing to do cleanliness, but just their way of breaking your will.

  4. Each day the prison official will throw 3-4 blank pages and a special marker to your cell. By the certain period of time you need to fill up those papers with every name and detail of every possible wrongdoing you MIGHT have done, or witnessed, or heard about. And if by the time he returns, if the pages are not filled on both sides with all the names, dates, locations, etc. you get beat up.

Beatings usually consist of them beating you with batons, they especially like beating the soles of your feet, your kneecaps, liver and kidneys.
When I was in jail the food was the worst thing over time. Any idea what their meals are like?

The most widely spread prison food is a so called "balanda." It's a porridge/soup that consists of potatoes, and God knows what else (rice, pieces of bread). Pretty much something you wouldn't eat unless you're about to die of hunger.

Inmates live off of packages sent by relatives, or whatever they can earn hustling and then buy off of guards. But again, it all depends on the prison. If you're in maximum security prison somewhere in Siberia or Far East, under 24 hour lockdown, you can forget about visitors/letters/packages. It's pretty much hell on earth designed to make your life as miserable and as short as possible. I guess its no wonder the vast majority of leadership of our criminal world (thieves in law) went through those "special" prisons.

On the suggestion of @pm_me_your_airbags (Ms or Mr), I'm posting a bug I encountered with my saved posts. @AmyAcker was able to provide a workaround. The full thread is here: https://voat.co/v/voatdev/comments/390732

Problem: I can access my saved submissions and comments by going to:
www.voat.co/user/USERNAME/saved

However when I click next at the bottom, it takes me to:
www.voat.co/user/USERNAME/saved?page=1

and shows my 'Profile overview' page.

Is there a way to access all of my saved posts, ie those on page 2 to and following as well?

Workaround:

u/AmyAcker:

I noticed this bug a while ago. I commented about it here.

Anyway, you can append ?page=1 to the end of the URL to see your saved post/comments. Just change the page number instead of clicking "next".
 

u/Rea11yN0tMe (i.e. me, the OP)

Great, thanks, that works.

I had also tried to manually change the URL to ?page=1, ?page=2 and so on, however the URL changes to a lowercase username when clicking next at the bottom of the saved page:

https://voat.co/user/rea11yn0tme/saved?page=1

and it only works when I change rea11yn0tme to uppercase like so:

https://voat.co/user/Rea11yN0tMe/saved?page=2

There it is, Ladies and Gentlemen. Happy hunting!
